extracted.intended_audience: women (ladies) learning or improving horseback riding; beginner-to-intermediate equestriennes
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructional guidance for ladies learning to ride and to manage horses gracefully and safely, covering rein handling, seat and balance, aids and defences, soothing/animations, corrections, common vices, and basic paces (walk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial rein hold (two hands)
rubrics_metrics.description: During first lessons: separate the reins and hold one in each hand, passing up between the third and fourth fingers, the ends brought over the fore-fingers and held by closing the thumbs; hands kept level a little distance apart, about three inches from the body, knuckles of the little fingers in line with the elbow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By slightly advancing the hands or relaxing the hold the horse will go forward; raise left hand to turn to near (left) side, raise right hand to turn opposite; slightly raise and approach both hands toward body to stop. When turning on one rein, the other should be slackened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced rein hold (both reins in left hand)
rubrics_metrics.description: As skill progresses hold both reins in the left hand, commonly separated by the fourth and little finger (or variations). Pass the off (right) rein over the fourth finger and the near (left) beneath it; carry the reins flat upon each other through the hand near the middle joint of the fore-finger, thumb upon them so their ends fall in front of the knuckles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elbow should be carried easily at a moderate distance from the body, thumb uppermost, wrist slightly rounded, little finger in line with the elbow. To make horse advance, bring thumb toward you until knuckles are uppermost and nails over horse's shoulder, then return gradually. Vary exact finger separation by personal comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand signals for turning and stopping
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific hand rotations change rein tension: to turn left -- turn thumb to the right, little finger to the left, and bring back of the hand upwards (left rein slack, right tight); to turn right -- nails up, little finger toward right, thumb left (right rein slack, left tight); to stop or back -- turn nails upwards, reverse knuckles, and round the wrist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These brief motions rapidly alter which rein presses the horse's neck or slackens; practice for prompt, graceful execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat: centre of saddle and avoidance of hanging
rubrics_metrics.description: The weight of the body should rest on the centre of the saddle; do not hang by the near crutch or bear weight on the stirrup; keep shoulders even and not advanced more on one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hanging on near crutch inclines body and head awkwardly; aim for ease without stiffness, and to rise/descend/advance/stop with the horse, not after him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posture of head, bust and shoulders
rubrics_metrics.description: Head in an easy, natural position (neither drooping nor thrown back, nor leaning sideways); throw back the shoulders, advance the chest, and bend the back part of the waist inward to produce an elegant bust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaning slightly backward tends to bring shoulders in and produces graceful confidence; leaning forward rounds shoulders and places too much weight on the withers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arms, elbows and hand carriage
rubrics_metrics.description: Elbows steady and kept near the sides in an easy position; the lower part of the arm should form a right angle with the upper part; wrist slightly rounded, little finger in line with the elbow, nails turned towards the rider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reins are held in one hand the right arm may depend easily and the whip held between two fingers and the thumb. Avoid squeezing elbows to the side or thrusting them awkwardly out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stirrup use and left leg position
rubrics_metrics.description: Stirrup chiefly supports the left foot/leg and assists rising in the trot; generally no weight of the body should be thrown upon the stirrup; left leg should descend gracefully by the horse's side and not be cramped or forced out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the near crutch properly (right knee over it, toes depressed, leg pressed against saddle fore) to help secure the seat; do not bear continuously upon stirrup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance as anticipation of horse's movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance consists in foreknowledge of the direction which a given motion of the horse will impart to the body and a ready adaptation of the whole frame to the proper position before the animal completes its action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When cornering or riding in circles lean back a little more than walking position and lean in the direction the horse bends; if horse shies or turns, keep time with his movements rather than pulling at the reins to preserve balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aids definition and primacy of the hand
rubrics_metrics.description: All motions of the body, hands, legs and whip that indicate the rider's wishes or assist the horse are 'aids'; those used to save the rider against a headstrong horse are 'defences'. The aids of the hand are considered most important and all others should assist and be governed by the rein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect harmony among aids is essential; a hand movement may be nullified by omission of appropriate accompanying aid/defence with body or leg (example: slackening rein when horse rears is futile without leaning forward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Body aids for advancing, stopping and rearing
rubrics_metrics.description: To indicate advance: incline body forward and press left leg (and whip if needed). To stop: throw body back gently proportional to severity. If horse rears: lean forward more than for the advance to throw weight onto fore-parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discretion with small mounts (ponies/galloways) when leaning forward to check rearing to avoid injury; always coordinate body with hand and leg aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of leg and whip as complementary aids and for turning
rubrics_metrics.description: Leg and whip correspond with each other; pressing with the stirrup leg can throw the croup and help a turn, while the whip can drive the croup out on the opposite side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase power of these aids as circumstances require; some horses need only slight pressure, others moderate or severe application. Combine leg/whip with hand and body movements for effective turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soothing: calm voice, still seat, and gentle bit contact
rubrics_metrics.description: To soothe high-mettled or fretful horses speak calmly, keep the whip motionless, maintain an easy steady seat and bridling-hand, and avoid making the bit press harder than necessary; relax the bearing as the horse subsides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfection of soothing is to sit entirely still and easy while remaining ready to perform defences instantly; avoid adding to the horse's animation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement: patting and caress
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement differs little from soothing except that it is advisable to pat and caress with the right hand while holding the whip in the left to coax shy horses to pass alarming objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use encouragement rather than force for shy or timid horses; repeat attempts only after the horse's fear has subsided and confidence returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animations: preemptive, light, and tailored
rubrics_metrics.description: Animations are intended to increase speed or liveliness without necessarily increasing pace; use slight movements, hand finger motions, leg or whip, voice and patting to rouse a sluggish horse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good rider foresees need for animation and uses it before decline in action; tailor intensity because what is a mere animation for one animal would be a correction for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: moderate, indirect, and dignified
rubrics_metrics.description: Ladies should avoid extraordinary correction or visible flogging; moderate corrections may be necessary, but severe flogging seldom helps. Best corrections dishearten and compel obedience indirectly rather than by direct force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid open contest; attack the horse's weaker side or use indirect, cool opposition and ingenuity; excessive indulgence leads a horse to domineer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling sudden restiveness/turning (vice of turning round)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a horse suddenly turns round (restiveness), do not attempt to prevent it with the weaker hand; instead pull sharply with the opposite (stronger) rein until his head makes a full circle, repeating several times with whip or leg if necessary, while preserving balance by inclining toward the circle's centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baffling the action repeatedly will discourage recurrence; do not try to force a failing aid with the weak side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to advance remedied by backing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a horse refuses to advance and whipping only increases obstinacy, make him walk backward until he shows willingness to advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backing can often succeed where punishment makes the animal more resistant or causes rearing/bolting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runaway management: keep together and guide
rubrics_metrics.description: In a runaway maintain seat and balance, hold reins so as to keep the horse 'together' (control his mouth) and guide him away from obstacles; sawing the mouth (alternately pulling each rein) or slackening then jerking may bring him up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dead heavy pulls; these may increase speed. After stopping beware the horse becoming disunited and possibly falling. Preserve self-possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with attempts to crush rider's legs against obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: If a horse tries to crush a rider's legs against walls or posts, do not fruitlessly pull him away from his chosen position; instead force him apparently to have his own way or attack his weaker side (e.g., pull head toward the wall while driving croup out) to back him away from the obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the horse's attack defeat itself; turning his croup outward can neutralize his ability to harm rider's legs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shying management
rubrics_metrics.description: When a horse shies at an object, slacken the rein on the side from which he shies and turn his head away rather than pull toward the object; soothe and encourage him to approach, repeating only after fear has subsided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pulling on the side he shies from (this increases resistance); coaxing and allowing him to examine the object usually reduces the fear; preventative turning of the head away can reduce starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stumbling response
rubrics_metrics.description: If a horse trips, immediately raise and support his head by elevating the hand and throw your body back to relieve his shoulders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not punish (whip) after a stumble: punishment makes many horses dash forward disunited from fear and encourages further false steps; habitual stumblers are often revealed by being punished after a stumble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rearing defence and prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: When a horse rears slacken the reins and bend the body forward to throw weight onto his shoulders; as he comes down recover position gradually and correct smartly or pull him round two or three times to divert him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevent rearing, foresee its intention and pull him round; be careful not to pull too much on the mouth while holding head up (may induce rearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kicking defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a horse tight in hand if it shows disposition to kick; while his head is well kept up he cannot do much mischief with his heels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rider is unprepared and the horse gets his head down, use reins and inclination of the body backward to prevent throwing; if opportunity allows, give two or three sharp turns to check kicking attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise progression and recommended practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginners should procure a quiet, well-trained horse and a careful attendant or groom; practise mounting, rein-holding, making horse advance/stop/turn, and proper disposition of body and limbs; some schools have pupils ride without stirrup or with arms behind while master holds long rein to settle seat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A friend or groom may materially assist a pupil; apply earlier observations progressively: one-third of preceding advice is directly applicable to absolute beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walk exercise specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the pupil walk the horse forward in a straight line at a slow rate, support his head to keep time in the beats, without holding the reins so tight as to impede the step or cause a trot; the hand should delicately but distinctly feel every beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If horse lacks exertion, animate somewhat; if he breaks into trot, check by the reins but not so firm as to stop; the moment he obeys and drops into a walk relax the hand. Practice turns alternately using both hands and slacken the opposite rein when turning; urge croup forward by leg/whip if horse won't bring it.
